chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: Back in Chicago and Little Bo's band again
summary: He tells of the Blue Room and meeting up again with Little Bo's fifteen-piece band and Sheila Guys.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So I had to come out here, see about my place o' business. So I had my sister runnin' it for me. 'Course, in the meantime, I went to Chicago. I lived seventeen years in Chicago. I got married in Chicago to a lady called Louella Brown. So we got together...Cut it off [the tape recorder].
So I left back East and come to Chicago. I ran into Little Bo's (?) band again. I run into Sheila Guys again. They was workin' in a nightclub there.
Who was in that band? How big a band was it?
They had about a fifteen-piece band...a bunch o' young kids. Been a long time ago. I don't remember none of them kids'
names. All I know is "Little Bo" (?). He was the leader. Little, bitty short cat.
He played the saxophone. He look like he about four feet...he's about the size of Mickey Rooney. Little, bitty short dude.
